title: Private VPC upgrade: fallback-proxy flow and offline validation requirements
creator: Sofia Reynolds
description:
Summary: Define requirements and acceptance criteria for a deterministic upgrade flow for Private/VPC deployments that supports (A) an optional customer-managed fallback proxy for controlled egress during upgrades, and (B) a verifiable offline validation mode for air-gapped environments. This ticket covers product-level requirements, operator UX expectations, telemetry and safety gates, and the acceptance test plan.

Background and motivation: Customers running Redwood Private in isolated networks have asked for a safer, auditable upgrade path that avoids surprise egress and provides deterministic rollback behavior. Existing upgrade docs assume either fully connected image repositories or a fully offline image import. We need a hybrid flow: allow upgrades when minimal outbound connectivity is available via a vetted outbound proxy or via a customer-provided artifact bundle with checks. The product must clearly state operator responsibilities, runtime checks, and SLOs for upgrades to be supported by Redwood engineering and SRE.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Operators can perform upgrades in three supported modes: Online (full egress), Proxy-assisted (egress only to a narrow set of endpoints via a customer or Redwood proxy), and Offline (air-gapped image bundle).
- Upgrades must include preflight checks, signed artifact verification, health-check-based canaries, automated rollback triggers, and telemetry sufficient for postmortem.
- Customers can opt into a fallback-proxy mode that allows short-lived, audited egress to fetch signed images/manifests when offline mirroring is not available.
- Acceptance tests exercise each mode and validate rollback, health thresholds, and no-unexpected-egress assertions.
scope_clarifications: We are not building a full image registry mirror service; customers remain responsible for mirroring images if they require fully offline upgrades.

Product will define a supported proxy handshake and a minimal allowlist of endpoints (manifest signing key server, Redwood image digest host) that proxy mode may reach; engineering will implement telemetry hooks and validation checks.
Console will surface an explicit upgrade plan UI with mode selection (Online / Proxy-assisted / Offline) and visibility into prechecks and expected downtime.
RBAC: only users with release-manager role may initiate a Proxy-assisted or Offline upgrade; Console and API will enforce this.
Support: Customer must provide a proxy URL + TLS cert (if proxy-assisted) or provide a signed bundle and checksum for offline mode.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Preflight checks run and fail fast if critical prerequisites are missing (mirror missing for offline mode, proxy handshake failing for proxy-assisted).
AC-2: Proxy-assisted mode: system performs a probe to the allowlisted endpoints via provided proxy; probe must validate TLS chain and signing key retrieval before upgrade proceeds.
AC-3: Offline mode: uploaded bundle is cryptographically signed by Redwood release key and checksum-verified by the runtime before any node image is swapped.

AC-4: Canary rollout: at least one replica group (configurable) must pass a health-check gate for N consecutive checks before full rollout; failure triggers automated rollback and opens a rollback ticket in Console.

AC-5: Rollback SLA: when automated rollback is triggered, the system must complete rollback to the previous version within 5 minutes for small clusters (<=10 nodes) and document time for larger clusters.

AC-6: No unexpected egress: during offline or proxy-assisted upgrades, outbound connections outside of the allowlist must be detected and flagged as a failure condition in preflight or in post-upgrade audit logs.

AC-7: Observability: upgrade events (start, preflight results, canary pass/fail, rollback trigger, completion) emitted to runtime logs and Console timeline; telemetry retention for these events is configurable per-customer.
AC-8: Operator UX: Console shows a dry-run summary (estimated time, nodes touched, artifacts to be fetched) and requires explicit acceptance to proceed with Proxy-assisted or Offline flows.
AC-9: Security: signing key usage audited; any missing or mismatched signature blocks upgrade and surfaces clear remediation steps to the operator.
test_plan: TP-1: Simulate a Proxy-assisted upgrade in a staging VPC: configure a test proxy that allows only the specified hostnames, run upgrade, and assert probes succeed and no other hosts are contacted.
TP-2: Simulate Offline upgrade: produce a signed bundle, upload via Console, run the offline path, and assert bundle signature and checksum validation logs are present and nodes boot the new image.
TP-3: Failure injection: block canary traffic during canary window and assert automated rollback triggers and completes within SLA; validate Console ticket appears.
TP-4: Egress detection: run packet capture during upgrade in proxy-assisted mode and verify no packets leave the allowlist; any deviation must cause test failure.
TP-5: Large-cluster timing: run upgrade on a 50-node test cluster to capture metrics for estimated duration and validate the Console estimated-time calculation is within +/- 20%.

TP-6: Post-upgrade audit: verify that all upgrade events are logged, include operator identity, mode selected, artifact digests, and that logs are queryable from Console within 2 minutes of event emission.
rollback_strategy: Automatic rollback on canary failure with successful health-check rollback path and logs collected for forensics.
Manual rollback: operator may initiate immediate rollback via Console; Console will surface affected nodes and estimated time for rollback.

Safe-fallback: if proxy-assisted mode fails mid-upgrade due to transient network, the system will pause, attempt reconnection for a configurable window (default 10 minutes), then rollback if reconnection fails.
operator_requirements: Provide a proxy endpoint with credentialed TLS and optionally client-certs when choosing proxy-assisted mode.
For Offline mode: provide signed bundle and checksum; ensure cluster nodes have the correct clock/synchronization for signature validation.
Approve Console dry-run and accept responsibility for any extended upgrade window when selecting Proxy-assisted mode.
